teaser.text: Sandisk Corporation turns NAND flash, memory that keeps data when power is off, into storage for devices, people and data centers. Its business is a chain: customers pay for products, Sandisk pays for memory and the work of making and selling them, and the difference depends on prices, contracts and supply.

blocks.heading: Where could Sandisk Corporation’s shares go?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $1,331.50 in October 2027, a 10% loss including dividends. It becomes $1,581.80 in October 2028, a 6% gain. By October 2029, it reaches $2,063.61, a 39% gain.

The bear case has a 30% probability. The base case has a 52% probability. The bull case has an 18% probability. These odds reflect the tension between strong current demand and an unusually cyclical earnings record.

blocks.heading: What could make Sandisk Corporation’s forecast work or fail?

paragraphs.text: The bear case falls to $3,000M, then $2,500M, before recovering to $3,500M. It assumes supply outruns demand, prices reverse and fixed Flash Ventures costs amplify the decline. NAND prices fell more than 50% in the last completed downturn. The bull case rises from $8,000M to $10,000M and then $12,000M, requiring enterprise demand to absorb new bits and BiCS10 to lower cost per bit. BiCS10 is claimed to improve density by 59% over BiCS8.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Sandisk Corporation really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending also has more than one useful definition because joint-venture funding, leases and wafer economics run through different lines. Inventory days rose from 135 to 178, and the cash conversion cycle lengthened from 136 to 162 days. Inventory deserves attention when prices can fall. Deducting US$232 million of stock compensation leaves “real free cash flow” of US$11,262 million, an allowance for dilution rather than another cash payment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Sandisk Corporation today?

paragraphs.text: A share price is not the value of the company. Market value adds up all common shares, while enterprise value adjusts that figure for cash and debt to show what investors are paying for the operating business. The forward P/E compares the price with predicted earnings, so its apparent cheapness depends on those earnings arriving. Enterprise value divided by revenue adds another warning: sales matter only if they become profit and cash.

earnings.opening: Sandisk Corporation's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. Watch whether shipment growth and realized pricing support the next outlook.
earnings.closing: The full Sandisk Corporation memo also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: For the next quarter, Sandisk forecasts revenue of **$10,300–$10,800 million** and non-GAAP earnings of **$44.00–$46.00 per diluted share**. Non-GAAP is management’s version of profit after removing selected items from GAAP, the standard accounting result. The exclusions include stock-based compensation: issuing shares may not require an immediate cash payment, but it dilutes existing owners. The forecast is therefore useful for judging operations, but it should be checked against GAAP profit, share count and cash flow.

Management’s longer-range model targets average non-GAAP gross margins of **80.0%**, operating margins of **75.0%** and adjusted free-cash-flow margins of **50.0%** across FY2028–FY2030. These are averages, not promises for every quarter. Free cash flow is the money left after operating needs and investment; the adjusted version also removes company-specific items.

blocks.heading: Has Sandisk Corporation kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Sandisk has delivered tangible results, including debt reduction and actual repurchases. At Investor Day on August 13, 2026, management promised to return all excess cash after investing in the business. That promise leaves judgment over what counts as necessary investment, but it gives shareholders a clear principle to test.

blocks.heading: How have Sandisk Corporation's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The eight-quarter sequence shows revenue weakening in early 2025 before climbing through the rest of the year and accelerating in 2026. Management attributed roughly one-third of sequential revenue growth to volume and two-thirds to pricing. That mix makes the quarter powerful but also exposes it to future price reversals.

Revenue and gross margin reached new highs, and operating income rose sharply from the year-earlier quarter. Because the recovery had already appeared in earlier quarters, the result is more than the disappearance of one accounting charge.
